newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union sets N. Irish natgas stake.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union sets N. Irish natgas stake.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co said Tuesday it agreed to acquire a 24.5 percent interest in BG Plc's (formerly British Gas Plc) Phoenix Natural Gas Ltd and Premier Transco Ltd subsidiaries.
Phoenix and Premier Transco are leading the development of the natural gas market in Northern Ireland.

Brooklyn Union, a natural gas distribution utility serving parts of New York City, will make the acquistion through its subsidiary KeySpan International Ltd, contributing $75 million toward's Phoenix's investment in Northern Ireland, manager of investor relations Jan Childress said.

Phoenix is building a natural gas distribution system and natural gas market, initially in Greater Belfast. Premier Transco owns and operates the natural gas pipeline linking Scotland and Northern Ireland.

Brooklyn Union chief executive Robert B. Catell said this joint venture "fits perfectly with our plans to utilize our expertise ... in international markets. We view our participation in Northern Ireland as a strategic investment in the same way that our active participation in the development of the Iroquois pipeline strengthened our distribution system."

Premier Transco transports natural gas through an 84-mile pipeline from southwest Scotland, under the Irish Sea, to users in Northern Ireland, including the 1,000-megawatt Premier Power Station in Ballylumford. Following conversion, the BG-owned power station is being commissioned on natural gas. The 24-inch Premier Transco pipeline now has the capacity to transport 300 million cubic feet of natural gas daily.

Phoenix Natural Gas has a license to distribute natural gas in Belfast and owns about 1,200 miles of unused mains and services. Previously, the Belfast system distributed manufactured gas, which was discontinued about ten years ago.

Phoenix is refurbishing the distribution system in Belfast by inserting new polyethylene pipes into the old system, and has so far laid more than 40 miles of new mains. The company has announced it proposes to invest $265 million.
Phoenix will be supplied with natural gas through the Premier Transco pipeline and through a 24-inch pipeline owned by Phoenix Natural Gas that runs from Ballylumford to Belfast.
Brooklyn Union said it will participate in the management of Phoenix Natural Gas and Premier Transco through the appointment of two members to the five-member board.

Brooklyn Union said it expects Phoenix Natural Gas will achieve a 60 percent penetration level in the domestic market over the next ten years. In government, commercial and industrial markets, BU believes a 40 percent market share will be realized in the same time frame.

"We believe natural gas will be the fuel of the future for Northern Ireland, and we will be able to take advantage of both the supply and demand side in this growing market for clean energy," Catell said.

In addition to the Phoenix Natural Gas distribution system in the Belfast area, "we see significant opportunities with BG Plc in Northern Ireland for pipeline expansion, cogeneration and conversion of electric-power plants to natural gas."
